analyst_view.overall: Bottom against top at the Alfonso Murube on Monday night: Ceuta are last with 5 points from 14 games (10 scored, 32 conceded) and have lost their last five, while Almería lead Segunda with 32 points (26 scored, 11 conceded). Sergio Lobera is in his first home game in charge after a 2-0 loss at Tenerife, and the club is giving season-ticket holders free tickets to fill the ground; Jordi Escobar (four goals) faces the club that signed him at 18. Almería coach Xavi García Pimienta warned that Ceuta keep the ball and play with intensity at home and that looking only at the table can mislead. Almería were last reported without captain Jorge Pulido (ankle) and Rodrigo Ely as well as Melamed (only Melamed is in the numbers); I found no fresh club update on Monday morning, so that rests on Sunday's report. Referee Eder Mallo Fernández (5.5 cards a game, near the league average) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, with Ceuta's share helped a little by last season's 3-2 home win in this fixture (+7.5% head-to-head from two meetings) and Melamed's absence taking about 6% off Almería. Ceuta create very little, but Almería reportedly line up without centre-back and captain Pulido, a starter the numbers don't weigh, which gives Escobar and Ceuta's attack a bit more hope; the two balance, so I stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.1 of them Ceuta's, already including their recent run of corners (44 in six, +11% momentum). García Pimienta expects Ceuta to keep the ball at home, which fits Lobera's possession game with high full-backs and that pattern; nothing in the news changes how many corners come, so 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards, already counting Ceuta's heavy recent booking (+12% momentum) and referee Eder Mallo Fernández, whose 5.5 cards a game is close to the league average (+2.5%). A desperate home side in front of a full ground may foul to stop Almería's counters, but that is the pattern the numbers already see, so I stay at 6.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.5 shots, with Ceuta's recent volume adding about 31% to their side and Almería's quieter attacking run taking about 7% off theirs. Lobera's side keeps the ball and shoots from range while Almería need few chances; a reshuffled Almería back line may let Ceuta shoot a touch more, but that is within what the numbers already give them, so 31.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. Ceuta hit the target only twice at Tenerife despite most of the ball, which argues lower, but Almería's back line without Pulido should make clean shots a little easier for them; those offset, so I stay at 10.3, with Almería's own accuracy already in the numbers.
